title: Deeper/broader consumer-backend and peer-evidence reconciliation
mode: Current project documentation/release research plus local plan cross-check
question: Which peer and FreeCAD routes can independently qualify the planned 2D, explicit-3D, and ACIS/ACDS claims?

sources.finding: Published FreeCAD DXF importer/exporter matrices give different entity and feature coverage to the C++ and legacy Python backends, including differences for LEADER, 3DFACE, block-contained annotations, text, dimensions, colors, and compounds.
FreeCAD documents that its native C++ DXF backend is not feature-complete and that DWG conversion uses external tools.
The mutable DWG wrapper routes through an external converter and intermediate DXF; import handoff checks expected output existence rather than exposing entity-level semantic success.
LibreDWG describes broad reading while noting advanced R2010+ skips, approximate converter coverage, and version-specific writer limitations; these are not per-entity semantic results.
The latest listed signed release remains v3.8.0 at 3a1c66b (2026-09-21), with an assembly-visibility change rather than a new solid-writer capability claim.
ezdxf distinguishes strict reading from recovery/audit, and documents recover.readfile as ASCII-only.
ezdxf states that unsupported ACIS nodes become NONE_ENTITY with data loss and arbitrary ACIS cannot be loaded and re-exported.

conclusion.implementationDisposition: Use existing focused local tests; add route/backend specificity to the already-scheduled composed qualification checkpoint only. Do not use backend exclusions as libdxfrw defects or promote claims from process success, recovery, aggregate counts, or wireframe projection.

limitations.notes: Source review only. Recheck mutable documentation and release identities before any optional composed qualification run.
